title: Card fraud screen: velocity, unknown currencies, rejects
scenario: A one-day batch fraud screen: transactions are converted to USD, scored by velocity / foreign-use / daily-limit rules, and given allow/review/block actions; unreadable rows are rejected with a reason.

verified.why_correct: Stripping every comma looks like it could break decimal commas, but the README says commas are thousands separators. '1,050.00' -> 1050.0 and '12,000' -> 12000.0 are both right; '12.5O' still raises ValueError, which is what makes T024 unparseable.

bugs.title: Velocity window drops the transaction exactly 10 minutes old
bugs.old: while state.recent and ts - state.recent[0] > VELOCITY_WINDOW:
bugs.new: while state.recent and ts - state.recent[0] >= VELOCITY_WINDOW:
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_velocity_window: T006 comes out ([], "allow") instead of (["velocity"], "review"). The c03 burst (all within 5 minutes) is still flagged.
bugs.why: T002 is at 09:00:00 and T006 at 09:10:00, exactly 10 minutes apart. The README keeps that inside the window, but >= evicts T002 before counting, so T006 sees only 2 transactions.
hints: How far apart are T002 and T006?
Look at the eviction condition in velocity_hit.
Evict only entries strictly older than the window: use >.
probes: Why does c03's burst still get flagged with the change in place?
What would happen if the deque were not reset per card?

bugs.title: Unknown-currency transactions silently skipped
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_unknown_currency: card c05 has no decision for T011 at all (only T009 and T023). The summary still says 25 loaded, so a transaction silently has no decision.
bugs.why: The handler catches UnknownCurrencyError and just continues, so T011 (ZAR) never gets a decision. The README wants it sent to review with an unknown_currency flag. Nothing else changes because the exception is raised before any card state is updated.
hints: T011 was loaded (summary says 25 loaded). Where did its decision go?
Follow what score_all does when evaluate raises.
In the except block, record a review Decision with the unknown_currency:<code> flag before continuing.
probes: Why isn't total_usd affected by this?
If to_usd were called after velocity_hit in evaluate, what else would this exception path get wrong?

bugs.title: ValueError handler catches missing fields first
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_rejected_rows: T015, T021 and T029 have reason "unparseable" instead of missing:card_id / missing:amount. The rejected count (5) is unchanged.
bugs.why: MissingFieldError subclasses ValueError, and except clauses are tried top to bottom. With ValueError first, every missing field is reported as unparseable and the MissingFieldError branch can never run.
hints: T015 has no card_id. Why is its reason unparseable?
Look at the class hierarchy of MissingFieldError and the order of the except clauses.
Put the MissingFieldError handler before the ValueError handler.
probes: Why is the rejected count right even though the reasons were not?
How else could you avoid this, without relying on clause order?

context_qa.a: It loads transactions.csv (getting loaded transactions sorted by timestamp plus a rejected list), cards.json and rates.json, then calls engine.score_all to get one Decision per scored transaction. It returns decisions, rejected and a summary.

context_qa.q: How does load_transactions decide a row is rejected?
context_qa.a: It calls parse_row for each CSV row. parse_row raises MissingFieldError (a ValueError subclass carrying .field) for the first blank required field, and parse_amount/parse_timestamp raise plain ValueError for text they can't parse. load_transactions catches these and appends {txn_id, reason}.

Each card has a CardState with a deque `recent` of timestamps. velocity_hit removes timestamps from the left that are too old compared with the current transaction, appends the current timestamp, and returns True if 3 or more remain.

context_qa.q: Where does currency conversion happen and what if a rate is missing?
context_qa.a: evaluate calls money.to_usd first. to_usd looks the code up in the rates dict, raises UnknownCurrencyError(currency) if it is absent, and otherwise returns amount * rate rounded to 2 decimals.

context_qa.q: Where is the daily limit checked?
context_qa.a: In rules.evaluate: it adds the USD amount to state.spend_by_day[txn.ts.date()] and adds the over_limit flag if the running total is above the card's daily_limit_usd.

c02 has three transactions between 09:00 and 09:10; c03 has three foreign (FR) transactions within 5 minutes; c04 crosses its 1000 USD limit with its third transaction; c05 has a ZAR transaction, and ZAR is not in rates.json.
